topic: All-season tires stop gripping around 45°F — rubber compound hardness, not tread pattern

beats.label: Hook
beats.visual: Extreme macro shot of a tire tread block on dry asphalt, soft natural daylight, shallow depth of field, no snow or ice visible anywhere
beats.negativePrompt: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles
beats.voiceover: This has nothing to do with snow.

beats.label: Setup
beats.visual: A minimalist analog temperature gauge world, needle resting near a marked threshold line, clean studio lighting, cool-toned background
beats.negativePrompt: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles
beats.voiceover: All-season tires stop working around 45 degrees.

beats.label: Value 1
beats.visual: Technical x-ray cutaway visualization of a tire tread block, internal rubber structure visibly stiffening, a cold blue tint creeping through the material, precise engineering aesthetic
beats.negativePrompt: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles
beats.voiceover: Below that, the rubber compound stiffens up.

beats.label: Value 2
beats.visual: Split-frame macro comparison of two tire tread blocks pressed against dry asphalt texture, one warm-toned and supple, one cold-blue-toned and rigid, studio product lighting
beats.negativePrompt: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles
beats.overlayText: GRIP DROPS — EVEN ON DRY ROADS
beats.voiceover: And grip drops — on dry pavement too, not just snow.

beats.label: Value 3
beats.visual: Premium product macro of a winter tire tread block, warm amber lighting, staying visibly flexible and supple, shallow depth of field, dark seamless background
beats.negativePrompt: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles
beats.voiceover: Winter tires use a softer compound that stays flexible.

beats.label: Value 4
beats.visual: The same analog temperature gauge world, the needle drifting slowly past the marked threshold line as the ambient light cools
beats.negativePrompt: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles
beats.voiceover: That's the whole difference — not the tread pattern, the rubber itself.

beats.label: CTA
beats.visual: Extreme macro shot of a tire tread block on dry asphalt, mirroring the beat-1 opening framing for a loop seam, light warming back to neutral
beats.negativePrompt: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles
beats.voiceover: Save this for when the forecast turns.

beats.label: SAVE freeze
beats.visual: Static hold on the CTA card
beats.overlayText:
Send this to whoever still runs all-seasons through January.
Stop by when it's time — we'll help you decide.

claimEvidence.claim: All-season tire rubber compounds begin to stiffen below roughly 45°F (7°C), reducing grip
claimEvidence.source: docs/REEL-SLATE-2026-07-31.md item #11 (pre-approved); consistent with published tire-industry consumer guidance

claimEvidence.claim: Grip loss below that threshold happens on dry pavement too, not only snow/ice
Winter-tire compounds use a softer, silica-heavy formulation that stays flexible at low temperatures
claimEvidence.source: general tire-industry engineering knowledge, not shop-specific
